text:
Situation: Leucovorin calcium has been on FDA's drug shortage list since 2012-01-01 and remains listed as of 2026-10-21, a duration of 178 months. Current inventory across our three sites provides 20 to 24 days on hand at present usage rates. Several leucovorin presentations at Corvale East show critically low days on hand, including the 350MG/7.5ML vial at 2.9 days and the 50MG/5ML vial at 2.7 days. Corvale Lakeside holds 24.5 days of the 50 mg/5mL vial. The rule-selected purchase option is American Health Packaging.

Why (FDA record): FDA posted the leucovorin calcium shortage on 2012-01-01. A labeled manufacturer, Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1021343), received an OAI classification on 2011-08-04, 150 days before the posting. That plant had prior OAI inspections on 2010-01-19 and 2011-06-17, and a Warning Letter on 2010-04-12. Another labeled manufacturer, West-Ward Columbus Inc. (FEI 1510690), received a Warning Letter on 2009-03-30 and a VAI inspection on 2011-01-20. FDA's shortage listing does not state a cause.

Our position: Supply is critically constrained for multiple presentations. The preferred vendor, American Health Packaging, is not on FDA's shortage list today, but its label does not name a plant we can verify. Four alternative suppliers share the same label limitation. No clinical changes are proposed here; those decisions rest with treating clinicians and the committee.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to place immediate orders with American Health Packaging for all available leucovorin presentations; requires Pharmacy Director approval.
2. Buyer to qualify Epic Pharma LLC, Ingenus Pharmaceuticals LLC, Leading Pharma LLC, and Major Pharmaceuticals as backup sources; requires Pharmacy Director approval.
3. Buyer to request plant identification from all five suppliers' regulatory contacts within five business days; requires Quality Assurance Manager approval.
4. Buyer to report weekly inventory days-on-hand by site and presentation to the Pharmacy Director until all presentations exceed 30 days; requires Pharmacy Director approval.

Not recommended: Switching to alternative agents or modifying protocols without committee review. Delaying purchases pending plant verification.
